Share of cooking energy input that ends up as internal heat gain in the dwelling. Cooking is strongly exothermic and its energy cannot all be captured by the food: the remainder leaves as sensible and latent heat. Only part of that reaches the zone -- an extraction hood removes much of it, and energy stored in the food leaves the balance when the food is eaten or cools elsewhere. 0.5 is a documented mid-range assumption for a dwelling with intermittent extraction, not a measured constant; raise it toward 1.0 for cooking without extraction, lower it for continuous mechanical extraction.

Share of domestic-hot-water energy recovered back into the dwelling as internal gain -- hot water standing in a sink or bath giving up its heat to the room rather than leaving down the drain. A real but small effect, and one whose size depends on drain-water heat recovery and on how long water stands before draining. Default 0.0 means not credited: the mechanism is parameterised so it can be explored, not assumed.

Useful cooking energy for one household-year, distributed across occupancy's own cooking_active hours. Derived from CBS's 2% cooking share of a ~1270 m3/yr average Dutch household gas use, at the calorific value and boiler efficiency in this same file (1270*0.02*9.769*0.9). Replaces the earlier practice of deriving cooking energy from the building's own simulated heating demand, which made a cooking figure inherit any heating error.
